Which generated pages are replaced by a static redirect, and where each one points. EMPTY TODAY ON PURPOSE: this commit builds the mechanism, and a set gains its paths at the step that is allowed to redirect them — RC-R4-1 fills `R4b`, RC-R9-1 fills `R9a`. A non-empty set IS the arming act, so arming a step is a one-file edit and a revert is the same edit back.

WHY REDIRECTS AND NOT AN HTTP 301. GitHub Pages serves this tree and has no redirect configuration at all, and shipped 0.2.x clients derive sibling URLs by path from `plugins.registry_url` (astra-daemon/src/plugins/registry_client.rs). So a moved page has to be a page: a canonical link for anything that indexes it and a meta refresh for a reader, written over the page that used to be there. ROLL-55.

WHAT MUST NOT BE REDIRECTED, and what refuses it. `registry/v1/*` and `transparency/moderation-log.json` stay byte-identical for as long as Pages serves anything (ROLL-55, ROLL-57): they are the signed documents and the machine-readable log that a daemon and an outside checker fetch, and a daemon that follows no redirect would read an HTML stub as a catalogue. `site/build.mjs` refuses a mapping that lands on either, and `site/selftest.mjs` compares their bytes across a build with redirects and one without, so this is not a rule somebody has to remember.

PATHS ARE SITE PATHS, as a reader types them, and a trailing slash means that directory's `index.html`. `<id>` and `<owner>` are the only placeholders; a key carrying one is matched against every page the build actually wrote, and the captured value is substituted into the target. So `/p/<id>/` is one line for the whole catalogue, and it cannot drift from the page count.

TARGETS ARE ABSOLUTE https URLs, never a base plus a path. The successor host belongs in exactly one place a reader can grep, and the astra-plugins-ops probe that fetches every target daily (OPEN-OPS-11) wants a URL rather than two halves it has to join. Table 5-F holds the successor for each page.

WHAT NOTHING HERE ENFORCES: that the workflow publishing the site passes `--redirects`. `.github/workflows/build-index.yml` does not pass it today, and while every set below is empty that changes nothing. `site/selftest.mjs` fails the moment a set gains a path and the workflow has not been wired, because a redirect set that never reaches the publish job is a takedown of the old URLs that silently did not happen.

sets.$comment: RC-R4-1. `/p/<id>/` → https://astra.minice.ai/plugins/<id>, and `/` and `/search/` → https://astra.minice.ai/plugins (search at /plugins?q=). Committed only after a probe shows each successor answering 200 (SERVE-84) and after ROLL-54's adversarial edge review of guest browsing is recorded — these are the redirects that send Pages visitors into a zone whose responses reach crowdsec (SERVE-105).

RC-R9-1. The other Table 5-F successors: `/publisher/<owner>/`, `/publish/`, `/policy/`, `/security/`, `/transparency/` (the page, never `transparency/moderation-log.json`) and `/advisory/<id>/`. Committed only after the same probe shows each answering 200. These pages stay on Pages until R9b, which is what keeps an old link leading somewhere.

ONE PAGE TABLE 5-F HAS NO ROW FOR, found by arming both sets over the committed catalogue and listing what was left: `404.html`. RC-R9-1's canary is worded "every generated HTML path is in set R4b or R9a", and with both sets full that page is the only one outstanding — so as worded the canary is red on the day it is written. It must stay outstanding: `404.html` is what Pages serves for a path that matches nothing, and redirecting it would send every mistyped URL into the service's guest zone, which is the traffic SERVE-105 and ROLL-54 are about. RC-R9-1 wants the exemption, named and reasoned, not a row in Table 5-F.
